entry.title: Lizzie Esau (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Lizzie Esau (pictured) covered a 1955 song for a 2024 series about a 1553 queen?

entry.title: his first film (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a Syrian filmmaker repurposed footage from his first film in his last film in order to criticize his younger self?

entry.title: Celeste Caeiro (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Celeste Caeiro's actions led to the naming of the 1974 coup in Portugal as the Carnation Revolution?

entry.title: Operation Blooming Onion (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Operation Blooming Onion uncovered instances of "modern-day slavery" amongst H-2A visa workers in the state of Georgia?

entry.title: a 57-year-old woman (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that L'Attaque, the board game that became Stratego, was patented in 1908 by its designer, a 57-year-old woman?

entry.title: Light Weight Air Warning Radar (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the Australian Light Weight Air Warning Radar was once loaded using canoes and later manhandled up a 200-foot cliff?

entry.title: Thomas Sewell (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Thomas Sewell said that in 2017 he attempted to recruit Brenton Tarrant, the perpetrator of the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings, into the Lads Society?

entry.title: abortion in Gabon (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that while supporting a law easing restrictions on abortion in Gabon, Prime Minister Rose Christiane Raponda said "it is not yet the right time"?

entry.title: the world's loneliest duck (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that "the world's loneliest duck" arrived on the remote Pacific island country of Niue in 2018?
